params.prompt: A hairline line drawing in one single red ink on pure white paper, in the manner of an architect's first site sketch made before anything is built: one confident continuous pen weight throughout, open linework, no shading, no hatching, no grey tones, no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos. Beneath the lines, one flat pale wash of warm sand colour laid loosely under the path and the building only, like a single marker stroke that does not stay inside the lines; nothing else is coloured. A few short dimension ticks along one edge of the path and one small registration cross in a corner, as on a plan. Generous white space. Portrait format. Redraw the attached photograph as this kind of line drawing, keeping its exact composition, horizon line, camera height and the positions of the path, the cyclist, the building, the grasses and the survey stakes, so that the drawing would register over the photograph. Subject: a newly paved public cycle path curving from the lower left foreground away into the middle distance, bending right past a low modern campus building with a wide overhanging flat roof and a long glass wall, loose strokes of tall prairie grasses either side of the path, a freshly cleared corner plot in the lower right with three survey stakes, one cyclist seen from behind riding away on the path in the middle distance, a few trees drawn as simple rounded outlines, a flat horizon with a second low building far off, the sky left as empty paper.
